text:
kevin: Heads up — saw sustained memory growth in KV cache for tenant T-82 during long-context runs (~50k tokens). Resident bytes climb steadily, fragmentation appears to increase, and eviction rate drops under long-lived pinning.

anya: can you paste the profiler snapshot?

kevin: quick pprof summary (30m window):
```
# kv_resident_bytes: 1.2GB -> 2.6GB
# top objects: kv_entry ~1.8GB (avg ~24KB/entry) -> many continued segments (slices)
fragmentation estimate: ~18%
evictions: 120/min -> 5/min during peak
```

kevin: interestingly eviction rate drops when ctx > 16k; looks like per-request cache pinning prevents shard reuse.

maria: any tenant_resident_limit set for T-82? noisy neighbors often pin hot pages via long streaming sessions.

kevin: defaults are unbounded (tenant_resident_limit = 0). some tenants have overrides but T-82 didn't.

sam: that explains it. plan: add per-tenant resident caps + fairness-aware eviction. quick experiment idea:
1) set tenant_resident_limit=512MB for T-82
2) change eviction policy to LFU-with-age (decay window=5m)
3) emit metrics: kv_resident_by_tenant, kv_evictions_by_tenant
run loadgen with heavy long-context tenant + many small tenants.

anya: loadgen command used:
```
./loadgen --tenants 100 --mix heavy:0.1,light:0.9 --ctx 50k --duration 20m
```

maria: after 10m with tenant cap 512MB we saw: 
```
kv_resident_bytes_T-82: 480MB
kv_resident_bytes_T-3: 220MB
evictions_T-82: 600/min
tail_latency_T-3: unchanged
```

maria: enforcing the cap prevented the heavy tenant from dominating and preserved baseline latencies for other tenants.

kevin: tradeoffs: more frequent evictions increased allocation churn and metadata overhead -> fragmentation initially rose, but a periodic compaction pass helped. We saw fragmentation drop from ~18% -> ~12% after compaction.

anya: compactor details?

kevin: simple background compactor that coalesces free segments across shard buckets. config used:
```
compactor_interval_secs: 900
compactor_max_work_bytes: 64MB
```
Performance impact was minor (~3% CPU spike during run) but reduced free-list fragmentation noticeably.

sam: follow-ups we agreed on:
- ship tenant-level resident metrics to Console + alerts when a tenant > 80% of its limit
- implement cross-tenant fairness: when choosing eviction victims, weight candidates by resident fraction so larger tenants are penalized proportionally
- support soft limits (90% threshold triggers aggressive decay window 1m) before hard evictions
- add integration test for long-context (50k tokens) multi-tenant scenario and a staging perf canary

maria: owners: kevin (implementation), anya (tests & metrics), sam (policy design). I'll schedule a perf canary on staging next week.

kevin: I'll open PR for resident cap + LFU-with-age + metrics; include opt-out for Dedicated customers. Cheers :thumbsup:

devbot: CI pipeline triggered for branch kv/tenant-caps — build started :gear:

sam: one more thought: consider tenant-weighted eviction knobs per deployment tier. e.g., lower tiers get stricter decay windows.

anya: agreed. also add dashboards for kv_resident_by_tenant and eviction rates, and an alert runbook for noisy neighbor detection.

maria: created tickets for metric export and compactor improvements. assigning refs in project board.

kevin: pasted the PR link in #eng-releases when ready. thanks everyone.
